after.1: He gave to everyone who asked. He kept his fires. He knew the Vedas to the last syllable. I told him, and told him. Now the lamp of our house is out.
after.10: I have nothing to give you for this. There is nothing in the world I could give you for this.
after.2: As Mandodari, walk across the field
after.3: You conquered your senses once, to win your boons. They have had their revenge. I asked you to send her back. I asked you every night.
after.4: She tries to lift his head into her lap. She cannot.
after.5: He stole another man's wife and broke every law. I do not know that I should perform his rites.
after.6: Enmity ends with death. Our purpose is done. Do it, with every honour. He is mine to mourn now as much as he is yours.
after.7: Rama, who may not enter a city until his exile ends, sends Lakshmana in to crown Vibhishana king of Lanka.
after.8: Rama is well, and Lakshmana. Ravana is dead. You can stop being afraid.
after.9: For a moment she cannot speak at all.
after.win.1: Lanka has a new king. Sita knows.
ahalya.1: On the road to Mithila they pass a hermitage. The trees are in flower, but no one lives here.
ahalya.2: Whose place was this? It looks kept, and it looks empty.
ahalya.3: The sage Gautama lived here with his wife, Ahalya. Indra came to her in her husband's shape.
ahalya.4: Gautama cursed them both. She was to stay here for years beyond counting, unseen by any creature, living on air, until you came.
ahalya.5: Rama looks, and where the others see nothing, he sees her.
ahalya.7: Colour comes into her from the ground up, like a lamp being lit.
ahalya.8: You are my guests. Sit. There is water, and fruit. It has been a long time since I gave anyone anything.
ahalya.9: Gautama, who has known this day would come, walks back out of the forest. He stands beside her.
ahalya.win.1: Ahalya is seen again, and Gautama comes home.
angada.1: One more time, before anyone dies. Go to him, Angada. Say: give her back, and live. Say it so he can hear it.
angada.10: As a rakshasa: tap to push the foot
angada.11: They try one after another, generals and princes. It is like pushing the earth. When Ravana himself rises, Angada steps back: "Touch Rama's feet, not mine."
angada.12: He heard it. He will not do it.
angada.2: I am Angada, son of Vali. You may remember my father: he carried you under his arm. Rama says: return Sita and ask her pardon, or I will leave the world without a rakshasa in it.
angada.4: Four rakshasas take hold of his arms. He lets them.
angada.6: He goes straight up with all four hanging from him, shakes them off like water, kicks the gold pinnacle off the palace roof, and is gone.
angada.7: Before he goes: the planted foot. (Later tradition)
angada.9: I will make it simple. Here is my foot. If any one of you can move it, Rama will go home without her.
angada.win.1: The last offer is refused. The war begins.

ashoka.1: Dawn. From the leaves of a shimshapa tree he sees a woman on the ground, thin, in one soiled cloth, like a flame nearly out. He knows her at once.
ashoka.10: If you are Ravana in another shape, this is cruel. If you are not, say his name again.
ashoka.11: I am Hanuman, messenger of Rama. He does not sleep. He sent you this.
ashoka.13: She holds it as if it were his hand.
ashoka.14: Climb on my back. You will be with him by tonight.
ashoka.15: I will not be stolen twice, even by a friend. Let him come and take me back himself. That is what is worthy of him.
ashoka.17: Give him this. And tell him what only he knows: at Chitrakuta a crow tore at me, and he took a blade of grass and made it an astra, and it chased that crow through three worlds.
ashoka.18: Tell him I can live one month more.
ashoka.2: Before he can move, the king comes, with torches and women, half awake.
ashoka.3: "Why do you sit in the dirt? You could have every jewel in the three worlds."
ashoka.4: "Your Rama is a beggar in a forest. He may be dead."
ashoka.5: "You have two months. After that my cooks will have you for my breakfast."
ashoka.6: You stole me when he was away, like a dog stealing from an altar. He will come. Look to your city.
ashoka.7: Say yes, fool, or we will share you out tonight.
ashoka.8: Eat me instead. I have had a dream. I saw Rama on a white elephant, and her beside him. I saw Ravana in red, riding south on a donkey. Ask her pardon while you can.
ashoka.9: They draw back. And from the tree above her, very softly, someone begins to tell a story: there was a king named Dasharatha...
ashoka.steady: She breathes, and stands straight again
ashoka.win.1: Sita has Rama's ring, and Hanuman has her jewel.

bharata.1: Bharata rides into a city with no lamps lit and no one in the streets.
bharata.10: Wait. If I asked Bharata for the kingdom he would give it. You know him. Wait and see how he comes.
bharata.11: As Bharata, walk up the hill to Rama
bharata.12: Our father is dead. He died saying your name.
bharata.13: Rama goes down to the river Mandakini, and offers water and the forest fruit he lives on. It is what he has to give.
bharata.15: "The throne is yours by birth. I am only keeping it warm."
bharata.16: "Our mother was wrong. A wrong boon need not be kept."
bharata.17: "The people are outside. They did not come for me."
bharata.18: It was his to give, and he gave it to you. I will not take back what my father gave away.
bharata.19: Do not blame her, or him. A promise is not kept only when it is easy.
bharata.2: Your father is dead. Rama is in the forest. The kingdom is yours. I did it for you.
bharata.20: Then give them a good king for fourteen years. They have one in front of them.
bharata.21: Then give me your sandals. Step on them once. They will rule Ayodhya. I will only carry out their orders.
bharata.22: Carry the sandals down the hill
bharata.23: He does not go back to the palace. In the village of Nandigram, outside the walls, he sets up a throne.
bharata.24: Place the sandals on the throne
bharata.25: Each matter of the kingdom is brought before the sandals first.
bharata.26: Two farmers dispute a boundary stone.
bharata.27: Send a surveyor, and feed both families until he rules.
bharata.28: Let the elders of their village decide.
bharata.3: For me? You have killed my father and made me a thief before the whole world. I will not have it. I will not have you call me son.
bharata.30: The spring festival falls in a year of mourning.
bharata.31: Hold it, quietly. The children should have it.
bharata.32: Hold it at the temples only.
bharata.34: The rains fail in the east.
bharata.36: Remit the year's tax, and dig tanks.
bharata.38: He wears bark and sleeps on the ground, and counts the years.
bharata.39: Rama leaves Chitrakuta, which reminds him too much of home, and goes south. At the hermitage of Atri, the sage's wife takes Sita aside.
bharata.4: He performs his father's rites. On the fourteenth day the ministers bring him the crown, and he sends it back.
bharata.40: You followed him. That was hard, and right. Take these: a garland, a cloth, ornaments. They will never fade or soil.
bharata.5: He sets out for the forest with the army, the three queens and half the city. At the Ganga, Guha sees an army hunting his friend.
bharata.6: If you mean him harm, you will not cross this river.
bharata.7: I mean to put him on the throne and take his place in the forest. Show me where he slept.
bharata.8: Guha shows him the flattened grass. Bharata looks at it for a long time. Then Guha gives him five hundred boats.
bharata.9: Dust, and banners. It is Bharata, come with an army to finish what his mother began.
bharata.win.1: The sandals rule Ayodhya, and Bharata waits.
boat.1: Shringaverapura, on the Ganga. Guha, king of the Nishadas, has been Rama's friend since they were young.
boat.2: Everything here is yours. Food, beds, boats, my people, me. Rule this place. You will be no less a king.
boat.3: You have given me the one thing I can take, which is your welcome. I have promised to live on what the forest gives.
boat.4: Night. Rama and Sita sleep on cut grass. Lakshmana stands with his bow, and Guha stands with him.
boat.5: He slept on gold and woke to music. Look at him. I have a bed for you too, prince.
boat.6: How would I sleep, with him lying there? Sit with me. We will talk until it is light.
boat.7: Go back, Sumantra. Tell my father we are well, and that we do not grieve.
boat.8: Guha brings the sap of the banyan. The brothers mat their hair with it, as hermits do.
boat.9: On the far bank, Guha watches until the trees close behind them.
boat.hint: Steer up and down. Hold right to row harder.
boat.pray: Mid-river, Sita folds her hands: "Mother Ganga, bring us back this way in fourteen years."
boss.deer.rule: Six arrows. It will not hold still.
boss.indrajit.rule: Thin hatching in the cloud shows where he hides
boss.khara.rule: Break the chariot; then one full, blazing arrow
boss.kumbhakarna.rule: His eyes, and only when he breathes in
boss.ravana.rule: Only the head in colour. Fill the sun to finish.
boss.subahu.rule: Two at once: fling one, burn the other
boss.vali.rule: Shoot only Vali, and only when he is clear.
boss.viradha.rule: No weapon can kill him: break both arms
bow.1: Mithila. King Janaka comes out on foot to meet them.
bow.10: I have seen it. I would not have believed it told. Sita is his.
bow.11: Let riders go to Ayodhya tonight. Dasharatha must come to his son's wedding.
bow.2: Sage, my house is honoured. And these two, who walk like lions and carry bows like grown men?
bow.3: Sons of Dasharatha. They have come to see the bow.
bow.4: Then they should hear how I came by my daughter. I was ploughing a field for a rite, and the blade turned up a child in the furrow. I named her Sita.
bow.5: She will marry the man who can string the bow of Shiva. Kings have come. None could lift it.
bow.6: It takes many men to drag it in: a long iron chest on eight wheels, and in it, the bow.
bow.9: It breaks in the middle with a sound like a mountain splitting. Everyone but the king, the sage and the two princes falls to the ground.
bow.win.1: The bow is broken, and Janaka gives his word.
bridge.1: The southern shore. Rama lies down on sacred grass facing the sea, and asks the Ocean to let his army pass. One day. Two. Three.
bridge.10: Tap in time with Nala to lay each stone
bridge.11: Fourteen yojanas the first day. Twenty the second. By the fifth, a hundred, straight as a parting in hair.
bridge.14: A squirrel wets itself in the sea, rolls in the sand, and runs to shake the grains out between the stones. The vanaras laugh. Rama picks it up.
bridge.15: He strokes its back with three fingers. Squirrels have had three stripes ever since.
bridge.3: Gentleness is taken for weakness. Bring my bow, Lakshmana. Today the vanaras will cross on foot, over dry sand.
bridge.4: Hold: a full draw, aimed at the sea
bridge.5: The water boils. Fish and great serpents flee to the bottom. And out of the waves, with folded hands, comes the Ocean himself.
bridge.6: Earth, wind, sky, water and fire keep to their natures, Rama. Mine is to be deep. I cannot stand aside. But there is a vanara with you named Nala, a builder's son. What he lays on me, I will hold.
bridge.7: This arrow cannot be put back. Where shall it fall?
bridge.8: North, on a coast where robbers drink my water.
bridge.9: I can do it. I did not like to say so before I was asked.
bridge.win.1: A hundred yojanas of bridge, in five days.

burn.1: They wrap his tail in cotton, soak it in oil and light it. They lead him through every street, which lets him see every street.
burn.10: He puts the crest jewel in Rama's hand.
burn.11: I have nothing to give you that is worth this. Only this.
burn.2: Then he makes himself small, and the ropes fall off. He jumps to the nearest roof.
burn.3: What have I done? The grove. If the fire has reached her, I have killed what I came to save.
burn.4: He hears the spirits of the air say: the whole city burns, and the daughter of Janaka is untouched. He breathes.
burn.5: He puts his tail out in the sea, and leaps north.
burn.6: On the way home the search party passes Madhuvana, Sugriva's own honey forest. They have good news and they have had a hard month.
burn.8: The keeper of the forest runs to Sugriva to complain. Sugriva laughs out loud. No one who had failed would dare.
burn.hint: Run and jump roof to roof
ch10.pray: Mid-river, Sita prays to Ganga for their safe return.

ch18.obj1: Fly close to strike the chariot
ch18.phase2: Ravana stands in the air and draws his sword.
ch19.again: Missed. The chariot turns in the wind; the hill comes round again.
ch19.landed: The bundle falls among the five on the hill.
ch19.obj: Drop the ornaments where someone will find them
ch19.trail: An ornament falls toward the trees.
ch21.obj: Taste each fruit. Keep the sweet ones for Rama.
ch21.sourNo: Not that one. It is sour.
ch23.hint2: Wait for the knots on every trunk to line up, then release a full draw.

ch25.m4: The fourth month. The sky clears.
ch26.mainaka: A golden mountain rises from the sea and offers him rest.
ch26.mainakaThanks: Hanuman touches Mainaka in thanks, and flies on.
ch26.simhika: Something below seizes his shadow and drags him down.
ch26.simhikaFree: He tears free. Simhika is gone in a burst of painted dots.
ch26.surasa: Surasa, mother of serpents: everyone must enter her mouth.
ch26.surasaBless: In and out, small as a thumb. Surasa laughs and blesses him.
ch27.seen: A guard looks twice. Hanuman slips back into the shadows.
ch28.remember: She closes her eyes and remembers Rama.
ch30.grove: Has the fire reached the grove? No. Sita is untouched.
ch30.more: More of the city must burn.
ch30.obj: Run the rooftops and set Lanka alight
ch36.north: Fly north to the mountain of herbs
ch36.obj: Carry the mountain back before dawn
ch39.obj: Light every lamp before the Pushpaka lands

coronation.1: Water has been brought from the four seas and five hundred rivers. Vasishtha sets the crown on Rama's head, with Sita beside him.
coronation.2: Lakshmana and Bharata stand to either side. Shatrughna holds the white parasol. Hanuman kneels at his feet.
coronation.3: Rama gives Sita a necklace of pearls, bright as moonlight. She takes it off, holds it, and looks at Hanuman, and then at her husband.
coronation.4: Give it to the one you are most pleased with.
coronation.6: The three queens are there. Kaikeyi stands with the others. No one in that hall looks at her differently, and Rama bows to her first.
coronation.7: Rama ruled for a long time. In his reign, the poet says, no widow wept, the rains came when they should, and old people did not have to bury the young.
court.1: He could go home now. But a messenger who has not seen the enemy's strength has done half his work. He looks at the pleasure garden.
court.10: Stand and wait for his answer.
court.11: Hold: coil the tail into a seat
court.12: He coils his tail under him until he sits as high as the throne. No envoy stands lower than the king he speaks to.
court.14: Brother, no. He is a messenger. Punish him, shame him if you must. A king who kills an envoy has no law left.
court.15: A monkey loves its tail. Set fire to it. Lead him through the streets.
court.3: He leaves one tree standing: the one she sits under.
court.4: Guards come in their thousands. He fights with an iron gate-bar. Ravana sends his youngest son, Aksha, who is brave, and a boy.
court.5: Hanuman admires how he fights. He kills him anyway, and is sorry.
court.6: Then Indrajit comes, and looses the Brahma astra. Hanuman could break it. He lets himself be bound: it will take him where he wants to go.
court.7: The court of Lanka. Hanuman looks at the king on his throne and thinks: if he were not so wrong, he could rule heaven.
court.8: I bring a message from Sugriva, king of the vanaras, and from Rama. Give Sita back. You know the law as well as any priest. Do not throw away all this for one theft.
court.9: Sit level with him first. (Later tradition)
court.win.1: His tail is to be set on fire.

dasharatha.1: Sumantra comes back with an empty chariot. The king asks one question: did he turn round? He did not.
dasharatha.10: "Rama. He was wearing bark. Did I see that, or dream it?"
dasharatha.11: "He did not turn round. He would not. I taught him that."
dasharatha.12: "The lamps are going out. Is it so late?"
dasharatha.14: At dawn the singers come to wake the king, and he does not wake.
dasharatha.15: Riders go north, to bring Bharata home from his uncle's kingdom. They are told to say nothing.
dasharatha.2: Kaushalya. Are you there? I cannot see you. Let me tell you why this is happening. I have never told anyone.
dasharatha.3: I was young, and proud that I could shoot by sound alone. One night in the rains I went to the river to hunt.
dasharatha.4: I heard water gurgle, like an elephant drinking. I loosed at the sound.
dasharatha.5: It was a boy, filling a pitcher for his mother and father, who were old and blind and thirsty.
dasharatha.6: I carried the water to them myself and told them what I had done.
dasharatha.7: You did not know, so you will live. But you will die as I am dying now: calling for your son.
dasharatha.8: Take my hand. I cannot feel it.
dasharatha.win.1: The king is dead. Bharata is sent for.
deer.1: A deer is grazing at the edge of the clearing. Its hide is gold and its spots are silver.
deer.2: Look at it. I have never asked you for anything in the forest. Catch it for me. When we go home it can live in the palace garden.
deer.3: There is no such deer. This is Maricha. He has killed kings out hunting with this trick.
deer.4: If it is a deer, she will have it. If it is Maricha, he has lived too long. Stay with her. Do not leave her for any reason.
deer.5: Where the deer fell there is a rakshasa, with an arrow in his chest. He draws one breath.
deer.7: It is Rama's voice, exactly. It carries a long way through the trees.
deer.intro: It lets him come close, and bounds away
deer.win.1: The sixth arrow strikes, and the deer is Maricha.

exile.1: Rama goes first to his mother. Kaushalya is at her morning prayers, dressed for her son's crowning.
exile.10: Before they go, they give away everything they own.
exile.11: Drag each ornament to a waiting hand
exile.12: Rama's crown-jewel, to a priest's son
exile.13: Sita's necklaces, to the women of the household
exile.14: Lakshmana's armlets, to an old soldier
exile.15: Kaikeyi's women bring bark cloth. The brothers put it on. Sita holds hers and does not know how it is tied.
exile.16: Sumantra drives them out. The whole city follows on foot, and at nightfall lies down around the chariot on the bank of the Tamasa.
exile.17: They will follow us into the forest and starve there. We must be gone before they wake.
exile.18: At dawn the people of Ayodhya wake to wheel tracks that lead toward the city and then are lost. They go home.
exile.19: By then the chariot is at the edge of the kingdom.
exile.2: Mother. I am not to be crowned. I am to go to the forest for fourteen years. I have come for your blessing.
exile.3: She does not cry out. She stands exactly as she was, holding the lamp, and the flame does not move.
exile.4: This is the work of one woman and one weak old man. Give me the word, brother. I will put you on that throne by noon.
exile.5: Put the bow down, Lakshmana. If I take the kingdom by breaking my father's word, what have I taken?
exile.6: Sita. Stay with my mother. The forest is thorns and hunger and sleeping on the ground.
exile.7: A forest where you are is a palace. A palace where you are not is a forest.
exile.8: And I walk in front with the bow. I am not asking.
exile.9: Go, my son. Think of Rama as your father, and of Sita as me, and of the forest as Ayodhya.
exile.win.1: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana leave Ayodhya behind.
exile.woke: A sleeper wakes. Sumantra backs the horses.
falls.1: Ravana rides out. Lakshmana meets him, and breaks his bow. Ravana takes up the spear, eight bells along its shaft, made by the architect of the demons.
falls.11: The sky begins to turn grey.
falls.12: He breathes. His face has colour. There are four herbs on a mountain in the north, between Kailash and Rishabha. If they are here before the sun, he will live.
falls.13: Hanuman is already in the air.
falls.2: It strikes him in the chest, and he falls.
falls.3: Ravana, who once lifted Mount Kailash, bends to carry him off as a prize. He cannot move him.
falls.4: Hanuman strikes Ravana once in the chest with his fist, and lifts Lakshmana as easily as a friend.
falls.5: Night. Rama pulls the spear out and breaks it, and sits down on the ground with his brother's head in his lap.
falls.7: "A wife can be found again. Friends, kingdoms. Not a brother born of the same father."
falls.8: "You followed me into the forest. I will follow you where you are going."
falls.9: "Do you remember the Sarayu? You could never keep quiet long enough to catch a fish."
falls.win.1: The night is nearly over. Hanuman has gone north.
friends.1: Mount Rishyamukha. From the top, the exiled monkey king Sugriva sees two men with bows, and is sure his brother Vali has sent them.
friends.11: Rama holds them against his chest and cannot speak.
friends.15: Lakshmana looks, for a long moment.
friends.16: I do not know the earrings, or the bracelets. I know the anklets. I saw them every morning, when I bowed at her feet.
friends.17: I had a wife too, and a kingdom. My brother Vali took both, and would have had my life. No one can stand against Vali.
friends.2: He sends his minister down to find out. Hanuman comes dressed as a wandering beggar.
friends.3: You have the arms of kings and the dress of hermits, and you look at this forest as if you had lost something in it. Who are you? I am asked to ask.
friends.4: Lakshmana, answer him kindly. No one speaks like that who has not learned the three Vedas. Not a word out of place, and not one too many.
friends.5: We are the sons of Dasharatha. My brother's wife has been stolen. We were told that Sugriva could help us, and that we could help him.
friends.6: Then I am Hanuman, son of the Wind, and you have just made my king very happy. Climb on my shoulders.
friends.7: Hanuman lights a fire. Rama and Sugriva walk around it, and are friends.
friends.8: Your grief is mine now, and mine is yours. And I think I have something that belongs to you. It fell out of the sky.
friends.win.1: Rama and Sugriva are sworn friends.

hint.roofs: Run and jump roof to roof
hint.row: Up and down to steer; hold Act to row hard
hint.shield: The shield blocks the front. Kick it aside, or wait for the swing.
hint.shootUp: Flyers: drag up to aim high
hint.shootUp.mouse: Flyers: aim high with the mouse
hint.shrink: Now tap to shrink, and dart in when her mouth opens
hint.walk: Hold left or right to walk

hut.1: Rama meets Lakshmana on the path, coming toward him, alone.
hut.11: A garland, broken. Wheel marks that stop, as if the wheels left the earth.
hut.12: Kadamba tree, you loved her. Did you see? Deer, where is she? You, river. Will none of you answer?
hut.13: Then I will ask no more. I will empty the sky of its gods and leave the three worlds dark.
hut.14: For one man's crime? You are the one who is patient. Be that now. We will find who did it, and then use the bow.
hut.15: Not far off they find the great vulture in a wreck of broken chariot, breathing blood.
hut.16: Ravana. King of the rakshasas. He took her south. I could not... I am glad I saw you.
hut.17: He dies with his head in Rama's hands.
hut.18: He was my father's friend, and he died for me as my father did. He will have a son's rites.
hut.19: Lay the flowers. Light the fire.
hut.3: She said things I could not stand and hear. I was wrong to go. I knew it as I went.
hut.4: They run. The clearing is as they left it, and it is empty.
hut.7: The doorway is open. The grass mat is still warm from the sun.
hut.9: The flowers she watered every morning, trodden into the ground.
hut.win.1: Jatayu has told them: Ravana, and south.
indrajit.1: An earlier night. Indrajit fights from inside a cloud, where no one can see him. His arrows turn to serpents as they strike.
indrajit.2: Both brothers lie bound and still. The vanaras stand around them and weep. In Lanka, Sita is flown over the field to see.
indrajit.3: Then a wind, and gold wings. Garuda, enemy of all serpents, drops out of the sky. The snakes are gone before he lands.
indrajit.4: Today he has gone to the grove of Nikumbhila, to finish a fire rite. If he finishes it, he cannot be killed. If he is stopped before the fire takes the last offering, he can.
indrajit.bossIntro: Indrajit takes to his chariot of cloud
indrajit.cp: The rite is broken. He rises from the fire in fury.
indrajit.end.1: Lakshmana: "If Rama is true, and has never turned from what is right, let this arrow find him."
indrajit.riteTip: The rite was completed. Clear the grove faster.
indrajit.tip: The coiling serpent tightens where you stand. Roll out before it closes.
indrajit.win.1: Indrajit, who once bound Indra, has fallen to Lakshmana.
install.ios: Tap the Share button in Safari, then Add to Home Screen. Open the game from that icon and it runs without the browser bars.
janasthana.1: Khara sends fourteen rakshasas first. Then he comes himself, with fourteen thousand.
janasthana.2: Take Sita to the cave in the hill, Lakshmana, and stand at its mouth. Do not come out, whatever you hear.
janasthana.3: You mean to meet them alone.
janasthana.4: I mean to be sure of her. Go.
janasthana.bossIntro: Khara drives at him in a chariot drawn by donkeys
janasthana.cp1: The ridge narrows. There is a cliff on either side.
janasthana.cp3: Khara's general Dushana comes up with an iron club
janasthana.end.1: The ridge is silent. One rakshasa, Akampana, is running south toward the sea.
janasthana.o3: Only one of them casts a shadow
janasthana.tip: Climbers come up the cliff edge. Stand near them and Rama kicks them off.
janasthana.win.1: In Valmiki, Rama fights the fourteen thousand alone.
janasthana.win.2: Janasthana is empty. The news is on its way to Lanka.
jatayu.1: Jatayu is asleep on his tree. He is sixty thousand years old. He wakes to a woman calling his name.
jatayu.2: Ravana! I am old, and you are young and armed and in a chariot. Still you will not carry her past me. Put her down.
jatayu.3: He lies where he fell, with his wings beside him, still breathing. Above him the Pushpaka turns south.
jatayu.bow: The mules are down. Now his bow.
jatayu.fall: The sword comes down twice. He is falling, and nothing will stop it.
jatayu.hint: Fly into the ring to strike. Keep clear of spears.
jatayu.phase2: The chariot falls away. Ravana stands on the air, sword in hand.
jewels.1: South, over forest and river. He holds her by the hair and the arm. She does not stop fighting him.
jewels.2: Below, on a hilltop, five monkeys are sitting. She cannot call to them. But she is wearing her ornaments.
jewels.3: The five look up, shading their eyes. One of them is Hanuman.
jewels.4: Then the land ends. Water, for a hundred yojanas.
jewels.hint: Tap to drop the bundle onto the hilltop
jewels.missed: It falls into the trees. Another hill is coming.
jewels.win.1: A bundle of gold lies on a hilltop, among five monkeys.
kaikeyi.1: Years pass. Dasharatha is old, and he has decided.
kaikeyi.10: "A crowned brother does not keep a rival near. Your son will be a servant, or an exile, or worse."
kaikeyi.11: "The king owes you two boons, from the day you carried him out of the battle. Ask for them tonight."
kaikeyi.12: Yes. I see it now. I should have seen it before.
kaikeyi.13: She goes into the chamber of anger, pulls off her ornaments and lies down on the bare floor.
kaikeyi.14: Who has wronged you? Tell me, and it is undone. I swear it by Rama, who is dearer to me than my life.
kaikeyi.15: You have sworn. Then hear the two boons you owe me. Let Bharata be crowned. Let Rama go to the forest for fourteen years, in bark, with matted hair.
kaikeyi.16: The king says nothing at all for a long time. Then he falls.
kaikeyi.17: Morning. Rama is sent for. He finds his father unable to speak, and it is Kaikeyi who tells him.
kaikeyi.18: Is that all? Then do not grieve, mother. I will go today. A father's word is not a thing his son lets fall.
kaikeyi.2: Tomorrow, under the star Pushya, Rama will be made crown prince. Tell the city.
kaikeyi.3: Banners go up. Lamps are set on every wall. No one in Ayodhya sleeps.
kaikeyi.4: From a rooftop the maid Manthara sees the lamps, and learns why. She goes straight to Queen Kaikeyi.
kaikeyi.5: Get up. You are lying on silk while your ruin is being arranged. Rama is to be crowned tomorrow.
kaikeyi.6: Rama! That is the best news you have ever brought me. Here. Take this jewel. I make no difference between him and my own son.
kaikeyi.8: "When Rama is king, his mother is queen-mother. And you? You will stand with folded hands before Kaushalya."
kaikeyi.9: "Bharata was sent to his uncle's house so that this could be done while he was away. Did you not wonder?"
kaikeyi.win.1: The crown is promised to Bharata, and the forest to Rama.
khara.chariot: The chariot is broken. Khara fights on foot.
khara.rule: Only a full draw will end it
kumbha.bossIntro: Kumbhakarna strides out of the gate like a hill that has learned to walk
kumbha.cp: The ground is shaking. The vanaras are running.
kumbha.elephant: Jump the charge. Shoot the rider.
kumbha.end.1: He falls toward the sea, and his colour goes out of him.
kumbha.end.2: No one cheers. On both sides, for a moment, it is silent.
kumbha.fire: A flame-tongue on the ground shows where fire will land
kumbha.grab: He has seized Sugriva. Shoot the hand!
kumbha.rule: Arrows cannot hurt his body. Wait for the breath, then shoot his eyes.
kumbha.tip: Watch his chest. When it swells, his eyes are open: shoot then.
kumbha.win.1: Kumbhakarna, who knew his brother was wrong, has died for him.
l1.10: Two men did this to me. And there is a woman with them. I have never seen anything like her. She would suit you.
l1.11: He is alone, and not alone. He has never been alone.
l1.12: Count the dead. One man killed fourteen thousand. That is not a man you provoke.
l1.13: She is your sister and she was maimed. A brother answers that.
l1.14: Did you hear how she spoke of the woman? You are already thinking of her.
l1.15: A hermit in bark cloth has insulted the house of Ravana. Who is he to you? Take what is his.
l1.16: Pride is the loudest. It usually is.
l1.17: He weighs it. And then, as always, pride speaks last.
l1.18: The Pushpaka sets him down at Maricha's door a second time.
l1.19: You will become a golden deer and draw him off. I am not asking for counsel.
l1.20: I see him in every tree. I hear his name in every word that starts with R. I beg you.
l1.21: Then I will kill you here.
l1.22: Then I am dead either way. Better by his hand than yours. I will go.
l1.3: Lanka, across the sea. A city of gold, taken by a king who studied the Vedas, sang to Shiva, and bowed to no one.
l1.4: Janasthana is gone, lord. Khara, Dushana, fourteen thousand. One man did it, on foot. He has a wife. Take her, and he will die of it.
l1.5: Ravana goes to the old rakshasa Maricha, who has lived as a hermit since a boy with a bow threw him into the sea.
l1.6: Who told you to do this? He is no friend of yours. Go home. Sleep beside your queens. Leave that lion asleep.
l1.7: For once, Ravana listens. He goes home.
l1.8: Then his sister walks into his court with her face covered.
l1.9: You sit there, drunk on yourself, and do not know that your own border is ash. What kind of king has no spies?
l1.win.1: Ravana has chosen, and Maricha goes to his death.
l2.10: Your people are watching how their king behaves. So are your sons.
l2.11: He could kill her. He cannot touch her. There is an old curse on him: if he ever again takes a woman against her will, his heads will split.
l2.12: You have twelve months to learn sense. Take her to the Ashoka grove. Guard her. Frighten her, if it helps.
l2.13: From a high window, Mandodari watches the girl led away. She says nothing. She has been married to him a long time.
l2.3: He shows her everything. The halls, the gardens, the treasury, the women who were queens before she came.
l2.4: All of it is yours. I will be your servant, I who have never been anyone's. What is a man in bark cloth beside this?
l2.5: She picks a blade of grass and lays it on the ground between them. She speaks to the grass.
l2.6: I am another man's wife. Tell him that the sun does not leave its light. Tell him to send me back while he still has a city.
l2.7: She said no. No one says no. That is why you cannot stop looking.
l2.8: She is a guest in your house by force. Every word she said was true. Send her home.
l2.9: She speaks to you through a weed. Break her pride.
l2.win.1: Sita is held in the Ashoka grove, and has refused him.
l3.10: He takes the enemy's part in your own hall. Your own blood.
l3.11: My uncle is the one coward born in our house. I bound Indra himself. Shall I fear two men?
l3.12: A kinsman is glad when his kinsman falls. If anyone else had said this, he would be dead. Get out of my sight.
l3.13: You are my elder, and I spoke for your good. Pleasant counsellors are easy to find. Guard yourself, and Lanka. I am going.
l3.14: He rises into the air with four companions, and crosses the sea.
l3.15: Ravana's brother, arriving on the eve of war. He is a spy. Kill him.
l3.16: He has come asking for shelter. If Ravana himself came and said "I am yours", I would not turn him away. It is my vow.
l3.17: He sends for sea water and, there on the sand, crowns Vibhishana king of a city that has not yet fallen.
l3.3: Lanka still smells of smoke. One monkey did that. Ravana calls his council.
l3.4: You conquered the gods, lord. What is a man, and some apes? Give the word, and we will eat them on the far shore.
l3.5: You should have asked us before you took her, not after. It was badly done. But it is done, and you are my brother. I will kill them for you.
l3.6: There have been omens since she came. Cows give no milk. The fires will not catch. Brother, give her back. It is not weakness to return what was never yours.
l3.7: He is right about the omens. A king weighs his city against his wish.
l3.8: Returning her now would be the first honourable thing in this whole affair.
l3.9: Return her? And have it sung that Ravana was frightened by a monkey?
l3.win.1: Vibhishana has crossed the sea to Rama.
l4.10: Keep the beat: six in a row will wake him
l4.11: He sits up, eats the hill, and asks who is at the gate.
l4.12: I told you in council what would come of this. You were wrong, brother.
l4.13: I did not wake you for a sermon.
l4.14: No. You woke me to die for you. I will, anyway.
l4.15: He is the only one who ever told you the truth and stayed. Do not send him.
l4.16: He is the strongest thing alive. Send him, and it is over by noon.
l4.17: That man spared you. What does he know that you do not?
l4.18: You have sons on that wall. End this before it reaches them.
l4.19: The brother speaks loudest, this once. Ravana lets him go all the same.
l4.3: I am your mother's father, and too old to flatter you. A king makes peace with an equal or a stronger. Give her back.
l4.4: I would rather break than bend. It is the fault I was born with. Go home, grandfather.
l4.5: He rides out himself, and for the first time sees the man. Rama cuts down his banner, his horses, his chariot, his bow. Then his crown.
l4.6: You have fought well, and you are tired, and you have no weapon. I will not kill you today. Go and rest. Come back tomorrow with a chariot.
l4.7: No one has ever spared him before. It is worse than a wound.
l4.9: He sleeps six months at a time, by a boon that went wrong. They bring drums, conches, a thousand elephants, and a hill of rice.
l5.10: You are a king, and learned in the law. A king does not kill a woman. Turn that anger on the man.
l5.11: Burn it all. Her, the grove, the monkeys, the sea.
l5.12: He is dead for a quarrel that was never his. Nothing you break now will change it.
l5.13: He turns back from the door. It is the last thing anyone talks him out of.
l5.14: Bring my spear. The one Maya made. And my armour.
l5.3: They bring him the bow, and nothing else. For once all ten heads are quiet.
l5.4: Hold his hand on the bow
l5.5: "He was the best of us. He beat Indra when he was a boy."
l5.6: "I taught him the rite. I told him it would keep him."
l5.7: "A father is not meant to see this."
l5.8: The lamp gutters, and is out.
l5.9: She is the cause. I will go to the grove now and do what I should have done a year ago.
l6.10: He sang for a thousand years, until he was forgiven, and given a sword, and a name: Ravana, the one who roars.
l6.11: The heads speak for the last time.
l6.12: You knew every verse, and what each one meant, and did this anyway.
l6.13: He will remember that you sang to him. It will not save you. Sing anyway.
l6.14: They all went before you. Do not keep them waiting.
l6.15: There is no one left to protect. Only a name to finish.
l6.16: You could still send her back. You will not. Then at least die facing him.
l6.17: You have known since Janasthana how this ends.
l6.19: You never touched her. You only wanted to be chosen.
l6.20: I am Ravana. I do not bend. I never learned how.
l6.21: Put on the crown. They should see their king once more.
l6.22: Send her back. I am asking for the last time. I have asked every night.
l6.23: He kisses her forehead. He does not answer. There is nothing new to say.
l6.24: He goes down to his chariot.
l6.3: Before dawn. His brother is dead, and his sons. The streets are full of widows. He is alone in a palace of gold.
l6.4: He remembers. Ten thousand years of austerity, when he was young. At the end of each thousand he offered one of his heads to the fire, like a lotus. He was reaching for the tenth when Brahma came.
l6.7: Let me not be killed by gods, or demons, or serpents, or spirits, or any of the great ones.
l6.8: Men he did not mention. It did not occur to him that a man could matter.
l6.9: He remembers Kailash. He tried to lift Shiva's mountain out of his way, and Shiva pressed down one toe, and he was pinned. He screamed, and then, because he was what he was, he began to sing.
lamps.hint: Light every lamp before the Pushpaka lands
leap.1: Mount Mahendra. He presses down with hands and feet until water runs out of the rock.
leap.3: The mountain shakes. Trees torn up by the wind of him follow for a while, like friends seeing a traveller off.
leap.4: He comes down on a hill outside the city, not even breathing hard, and looks at the walls of gold.
leap.mainaka: A golden mountain rises from the sea: "Rest on me, son of the Wind."
leap.mainaka2: He touches the peak with his hand, in thanks. "I have promised not to stop."
leap.simhika2: She is gone, in a burst
leap.surasa: Surasa, mother of serpents: "No one passes who does not enter my mouth."
leap.surasa2: She opens wider than he can grow
leap.surasa3: "You have been in my mouth. Go, and succeed."
leap.win.1: A hundred yojanas of sea are behind him.
lighting.1: Fourteen years, to the day. Vibhishana gives them the Pushpaka. It carries them north, and Rama points down.
lighting.10: "That clearing. Our hut is still standing."
lighting.12: "Chitrakuta, where Bharata came. And the Ganga, and Guha's town."
lighting.13: Hanuman goes ahead. Bharata had sworn to walk into fire if Rama was a day late. He is thin, and in bark, and has been counting.
lighting.14: He is at Bharadvaja's hermitage tonight. He will be here tomorrow.
lighting.15: After so long. They say joy comes to a man who lives, if he waits a hundred years. It is true.
lighting.16: Bharata comes out barefoot, with the sandals on his head. He kneels, and puts them on his brother's feet.
lighting.17: Here is your kingdom. I kept it for you. It is ten times what you left.
lighting.18: Ayodhya has one night to make ready.
lighting.2: Tap each place as it passes below
lighting.4: "There is Nala's bridge. And there I lay three days asking the sea."
lighting.6: "Kishkindha. Let us stop for Tara and the vanara wives. They should see Ayodhya."
lighting.8: "Pampa, where I wept. And Shabari's hut."
lighting.win.1: Every lamp in Ayodhya is lit.
lose.rite: The rite is complete. Indrajit cannot be stopped now.
motif.1.name: The double line
motif.1.text: Old Mithila figures are drawn with two parallel outlines and colour laid between them. Every figure in this game is drawn that way.
motif.10.name: Natural colour
motif.10.text: The old palette came from the house and the field: lampblack, turmeric, indigo, the red of kusum flowers, green from leaves, white from rice. This game uses no colour outside it.
motif.2.name: Bharni and kachni
motif.2.text: Bharni is filling: flat, bold colour. Kachni is line: fine hatching with little colour. Here the world is kachni until you free it, and what you play is bharni. Lanka is kachni throughout.
motif.3.name: Lotus and bamboo
motif.3.text: The lotus ring pierced by a bamboo stem is the centre of the kohbar, the painting made on the wall of the bridal room. It stands for the union of bride and groom and the wish for children.
motif.4.name: Fish
motif.4.text: Fish are signs of plenty and good fortune, and are painted wherever there is space to fill.
motif.5.name: Parrots
motif.5.text: Parrots, often in pairs, are the birds of love in kohbar paintings.
motif.6.name: Sun and moon
motif.6.text: The sun and moon are painted as witnesses to a marriage and as a wish for long life.
motif.7.name: Naina-jogin
motif.7.text: Four veiled women painted in the corners of the bridal room, to watch over the couple and turn away the evil eye. In this game they sit in the corners of the screen and lift their eyes when the hero is close to falling.
motif.8.name: Aripan
motif.8.text: Floor drawings made with rice paste by the women of the house on feast days. The astra symbols, the aim line of the bow and the line around the hut are drawn in that white.
motif.9.name: The border
motif.9.text: Mithila walls and papers are framed with bands of triangles, zigzags and vines. No space is left bare: empty ground is filled with flowers, birds and dots.
night.1: He waits for dark, and makes himself the size of a cat.
night.2: I am Lanka. I am this city. No one comes in past me, little monkey.
night.3: Strike once, with the left fist
night.4: Brahma told me: when a monkey strikes you down, know that the end of the rakshasas has come. Go in. Do what you came for.
night.5: In the inner palace the king sleeps among his queens. One lies apart, in gold, so beautiful that Hanuman thinks: I have found her.
night.6: Then he thinks again. She would not sleep. She would not eat. She would not wear gold in this house. That is Mandodari.
night.7: He has looked in every room in Lanka. If she is dead, how can he go back and say so?
night.8: There is a grove I have not searched. Ashoka trees, behind a wall.
night.hint: Move. Hold Hide beside a pot or pillar.
night.seen: A guard turns. Back to the last hiding place.
night.win.1: He has searched all Lanka but one grove.
note.after.1: Vibhishana's lament, Mandodari's, and Rama's answer that enmity ends with death are in Valmiki. Vibhishana is crowned by Lakshmana, and Hanuman carries the news to Sita.
note.after.2: What follows next in Valmiki is not shown in this version of the game. Sita is brought before Rama, and his words lead her to enter a fire to prove her purity; Agni, the god of fire, returns her unharmed. It is the most debated scene in the epic, and the makers have not yet decided how to show it.
note.ahalya.1: In Valmiki, Ahalya is not turned to stone. She is cursed to live in the hermitage invisible to all, doing penance, until Rama arrives. Rama and Lakshmana touch her feet as they would an elder's, and she receives them as guests.
note.ahalya.2: The well-known version in which she is a stone that comes alive at the touch of Rama's foot comes from later tellings.
note.angada.1: In Valmiki, Rama sends Angada with a final offer. Ravana orders him seized; Angada leaps up with his captors clinging to him, shakes them off, breaks the pinnacle of the palace and returns.
note.angada.2: The famous scene in which Angada plants his foot and no one in Ravana's court can move it comes from later tellings. It is offered here as an optional moment and labelled.
note.ashoka.1: Ravana's visit and his two-month threat, the blade of grass, Trijata's dream, Hanuman's way of making himself known by telling Rama's story, the ring, the crest jewel and the story of the crow are all in Valmiki.
note.ashoka.2: So is Sita's refusal to be carried back: Rama himself must come.
note.bharata.1: Bharata's refusal of the throne, Guha's suspicion at the river, the meeting at Chitrakuta and the rule of the sandals from Nandigram are all Valmiki. So is Anasuya's gift to Sita.
note.bharata.2: The three small rulings are the game's invention, to let the player feel how Bharata governed: always in his brother's name.
note.boat.1: Guha, king of the forest-dwelling Nishadas, is Rama's friend and equal in Valmiki. He offers Rama his kingdom, keeps watch all night with Lakshmana and weeps to see Rama on the ground. Mid-river, Sita prays to the Ganga for their safe return.
note.boat.2: The well-loved boatman who insists on washing Rama's feet comes from Tulsidas, centuries later, and is not used here.
note.bow.1: Valmiki describes the bow arriving in an iron chest on eight wheels, pulled by a great many men. Rama lifts it, strings it and draws it, and it snaps in two.
note.bow.2: The text has no contest among assembled suitors; that scene, the swayamvara, comes from later tellings. Here Janaka simply tells of the kings who tried before.
note.bridge.1: Rama's three-day vigil, his anger, the Ocean's appearance and advice, and Nala's bridge built in five days are in Valmiki. The arrow, once drawn, is loosed at a distant coast.
note.bridge.2: The squirrel whose back Rama strokes, and the stones that float because his name is written on them, come from later tellings. The squirrel is offered here as an optional moment and labelled.
note.burn.1: The burning of Lanka, Hanuman's sudden fear that he has burned Sita too, the raid on the honey forest Madhuvana and Sugriva's delight at it, and Hanuman's first words to Rama are all in Valmiki. Rama says he has nothing to give Hanuman in return but an embrace.
note.coronation.1: Valmiki's Yuddha Kanda ends with the coronation. Sita's gift of the pearl necklace to Hanuman, with Rama's consent, is in the text, and so is the description of Rama's reign.
note.coronation.2: The Uttara Kanda, a seventh book which many scholars consider a later addition, continues the story. This game ends where the six kandas end.
note.court.1: Hanuman wrecks the grove on purpose to measure Lanka's strength, kills Ravana's young son Aksha, and lets Indrajit's Brahma astra bind him. His thought on first seeing Ravana enthroned is Valmiki's. So is Vibhishana's objection that an envoy may not be killed.
note.court.2: The coiled-tail seat as high as Ravana's throne comes from later tellings, and is offered here as an optional moment.
note.dasharatha.1: On the sixth night after Rama leaves, Valmiki has Dasharatha tell Kaushalya of the young ascetic he killed by mistake, and of the curse laid on him by the boy's blind father. He dies that night.
note.dasharatha.2: The boy is not named in Valmiki. He is called Shravana in later tellings.
note.deer.1: In Valmiki, Lakshmana says at once that the deer is Maricha. Rama goes anyway, reasoning that either Sita will have her deer or a dangerous rakshasa will be dead. Maricha leads him far from the hut, and dying, cries out in Rama's voice for Sita and Lakshmana.
note.exile.1: All of this is in Valmiki: Lakshmana's anger, Sita's refusal to stay, Sumitra's blessing, the giving away of their wealth, and the night at the Tamasa, where Rama has Sumantra drive in circles so the sleeping citizens cannot follow the tracks.
note.exile.2: Sita's line about the forest and the palace is the game's short form of a long speech.
note.falls.1: In Valmiki it is Ravana's spear, the shakti, that fells Lakshmana, after Indrajit's death. Ravana tries to lift him and cannot; Hanuman strikes Ravana and carries Lakshmana to Rama.
note.falls.2: Rama's lament, that a wife or a kingdom can be found again but not a brother, is from the text.
note.friends.1: Rama's praise of Hanuman's speech, the friendship sworn around a fire, and the bundle of ornaments are all Valmiki.
note.friends.2: So is Lakshmana's answer about the anklets, one of the best-known lines in the poem.
note.hut.1: Rama's search, his questions to the trees and animals, and his threat to destroy the worlds are a long and famous passage of Valmiki. It is Lakshmana who calms him.
note.hut.2: Rama performs Jatayu's funeral himself, with the rites due to a father.
note.indrajit.1: Vibhishana reveals that Indrajit can be killed only if his rite at Nikumbhila is interrupted. Lakshmana breaks it and, after a long duel, looses the Aindra astra with an oath on Rama's truthfulness.
note.indrajit.2: Indrajit fought on several earlier days. He bound the brothers with serpent arrows until Garuda freed them, and once struck down an illusion of Sita to break the vanaras' spirit. The game shows only the serpent arrows and the last fight.
note.janasthana.1: Valmiki is explicit that Rama sends Lakshmana and Sita to a cave and fights Khara's army of fourteen thousand by himself, on foot. He kills the generals Dushana and Trishiras, destroys Khara's chariot, and ends the battle with a single blazing arrow given to him by Agastya.
note.janasthana.2: Akampana's escape to Lanka is told at the opening of the next part of the kanda.
note.jatayu.1: Valmiki gives the old vulture a real fight. Jatayu kills the charioteer and the mules, wrecks the chariot, breaks Ravana's bow and tears at his arms, before Ravana cuts off his wings with his sword.
note.jatayu.2: He does not die at once. He lives long enough to tell Rama which way she was taken.
note.jewels.1: In Valmiki, Sita sees five vanaras on a mountain top, ties her ornaments in her upper cloth and drops them, hoping they will tell Rama. Ravana, in his hurry, does not notice.
note.jewels.2: Sugriva keeps the bundle. It matters later.
note.kaikeyi.1: Valmiki shows Kaikeyi at first overjoyed at Rama's crowning; she rewards Manthara for the news. It is Manthara's long argument that turns her. The two boons date from a battle in which Kaikeyi saved the king's life.
note.kaikeyi.2: The chariot-wheel brooch Kaikeyi wears in this game nods to a later folk story that she saved him by holding his chariot wheel together. That detail is not in Valmiki.
note.kumbhakarna.1: In Valmiki, Kumbhakarna scatters the vanara army and carries off Sugriva, who escapes. Rama then kills him.
note.kumbhakarna.2: The text describes that death in detail: his arms, legs and head are cut away by arrows. The game shows only a fall. The rule about his eyes and his breath is a game device and is not in the poem.
note.l1.1: This follows Valmiki closely. Akampana brings the news; Maricha talks Ravana out of it once; Shurpanakha then shames him in open court and describes Sita; and Ravana returns to Maricha with a threat. Maricha's line that he would rather die at Rama's hands is in the text.
note.l1.2: The ten heads arguing among themselves are the game's device for showing a mind at odds with itself. No choice here changes what happens next.
note.l2.1: The tour of the palace, the blade of grass that Sita places between them, and the deadline of twelve months are in Valmiki's Aranya Kanda.
note.l2.2: The curse that keeps Ravana from forcing her is told in the Uttara Kanda, which many scholars consider a later addition to the poem. It is mentioned here in one line, and labelled.
note.l3.1: The council, Kumbhakarna's blunt criticism followed by his loyalty, Vibhishana's advice, Indrajit's mockery and Ravana's insult are in Valmiki. Vibhishana leaves with four companions.
note.l3.2: On the shore Sugriva wants him killed as a spy. Rama's answer, that he will not refuse anyone who asks for refuge, is one of the central statements of the poem.
note.l4.1: Malyavan's plea, Ravana's first meeting with Rama (who destroys his chariot and crown and sends him home to rest), and the long comic labour of waking Kumbhakarna are in Valmiki.
note.l4.2: Kumbhakarna tells his brother plainly that he was wrong, and then goes out to fight for him. The words used here are the game's; the meaning is the text's.
note.l5.1: Ravana's lament for Indrajit is in Valmiki, and so is what follows it: in his rage he sets out to kill Sita, and his minister Suparshva stops him, saying that a king does not kill a woman and that he should turn his anger on Rama.
note.l5.2: The ten heads are the game's device.
note.l6.1: This chapter is mostly not from Valmiki's six kandas. Ravana's ten thousand years of austerity, the offering of his heads, Brahma's boon that left out mankind, and his pinning under Mount Kailash are told in the Uttara Kanda, which many scholars consider a later addition to the poem.
note.l6.2: The game shows the heads as lotuses laid in a fire. The last conversation with Mandodari is the game's own scene, drawn from her lament after his death, where she says she warned him.
note.leap.1: The leap opens the Sundara Kanda. The mountain Mainaka rises to offer rest, and Hanuman touches it and flies on. The gods send Surasa to test him; he makes himself huge, then tiny, slips in and out of her mouth, and is blessed. The demoness Simhika, who catches creatures by their shadows, he kills.
note.lighting.1: The flight home in the Pushpaka, with Rama pointing out to Sita each place they pass, Hanuman's errand to Bharata, and Bharata placing the sandals on Rama's feet are in Valmiki.
note.lighting.2: The custom of lighting lamps to welcome Rama home is popular tradition, kept across India as Diwali. It is not described in the poem.
note.night.1: Hanuman shrinks to the size of a cat, strikes down the guardian Lankini with his left fist, and searches the city by night. In the palace he mistakes Mandodari for Sita, then reasons that Sita would never sleep at ease in Ravana's house.
note.night.2: His despair before he notices the Ashoka grove is one of the most human passages in the kanda.
note.ravana.1: Indra's chariot and its driver Matali, the heads that grow back as fast as Rama cuts them down, Matali's reminder, and the Brahma astra that strikes Ravana in the chest are all in Valmiki. Agastya's teaching of the Aditya Hridayam is in most recensions, though some editors consider it an early addition.
note.ravana.2: The idea that Ravana's life was hidden in his navel comes from later tellings and is not used.
note.rekha.1: The abduction is Valmiki: the cry, Sita's harsh words to Lakshmana, his leaving against his own judgement, Ravana's disguise as a wandering ascetic, and Sita's call to the trees and the river.
note.rekha.2: The line is later tradition. In Valmiki, Lakshmana leaves without drawing anything. The Lakshmana Rekha appears in later tellings and is alluded to in Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas (that passage should be checked by a reviewer). The game keeps it because so many people know the story this way, and shows Sita's step as an act of duty to a guest, which is how the older text frames her welcome.
note.sage.1: In Valmiki, Dasharatha first promises Vishvamitra anything, then refuses when he hears the request, and offers his army and himself instead. The sage grows angry. It is Vasishtha who persuades the king to let Rama go.
note.sage.2: Lakshmana goes too, without being asked.
note.sala.1: Both proofs are in Valmiki: the skeleton of Dundubhi flicked away with a toe, and then, because Sugriva points out that it has dried, a single arrow through seven sala trees.
note.sanjeevani.1: Unable to find the herbs, which hide themselves, Hanuman tears up the whole peak and brings it. In Valmiki he does this twice in the war: once after Indrajit strikes down the whole army, and once for Lakshmana.
note.sanjeevani.2: The idea that he must return before sunrise comes from later tellings. The game uses it only as a timer.
note.sarayu.1: Valmiki has the sage teach Rama the mantras Bala and Atibala on the bank of the Sarayu. The archery practice is the game's own addition, to teach the bow.
note.sarayu.2: Rama's doubt about killing a woman is in the text, and so is the sage's answer.
note.search.1: The rains, Lakshmana's anger and Tara's good sense, the gift of the ring, the cave of Svayamprabha, the despair on the shore, Sampati, and Jambavan's speech to Hanuman all follow Valmiki.
note.search.2: Rama's lines during the rains are a few of the many images from that long passage.
note.shabari.1: Kabandha, Shabari's long wait, her welcome and her ascent through the fire are in Valmiki. She is an ascetic honoured by Rama, and he praises her.
note.shabari.2: In Valmiki she offers fruit she has gathered. The detail that she tasted each berry first, to be sure it was sweet, is later tradition and one of the most loved stories in the Ramayana; the game uses it and says so.
note.shurpanakha.1: Valmiki shows this plainly. Rama teases Shurpanakha and sends her to Lakshmana, who mocks her and sends her back. When she attacks Sita, Rama tells Lakshmana to disfigure her, and he cuts off her nose and ears.
note.shurpanakha.2: The game shows the wound only as a veil and a cry. It does not soften what the text says the brothers did.
note.tataka.1: In Valmiki's telling, Tataka was born a yakshini, strong as a thousand elephants, and was cursed to become a rakshasi. She emptied the lands around her of people. When Rama faced her she raised dust, rained stones and made herself invisible. Rama tried at first only to stop her; Vishvamitra urged him to finish before dusk, and one arrow ended the fight. It is Rama's first battle, and the sage rewards him with the astras.
note.vali.1: This is one of the most debated moments in the epic, and the game gives Valmiki's account without softening it. Rama shoots Vali from concealment while Vali is fighting Sugriva. The dying Vali accuses him at length. Rama answers that Vali had taken his brother's wife and that he acted as a king's agent in punishing it. Vali accepts the answer and entrusts Angada to him.
note.vali.2: Readers have argued about that answer for two thousand years.
note.viradha.1: Viradha, in Valmiki, carries Sita off and boasts that no weapon can kill him. The brothers break his arms, and he asks to be buried; he was a gandharva under a curse. Sita's warning to Rama about the bow is also in the text.
note.viradha.2: The ten years among the hermitages, Agastya's gift of Vishnu's bow, and the meeting with Jatayu at Panchavati follow, as shown.
note.wedding.1: Valmiki marries all four brothers at once: Rama to Sita, Lakshmana to Urmila, and Bharata and Shatrughna to Janaka's nieces Mandavi and Shrutakirti. On the way home Parashurama challenges Rama with Vishnu's bow, is humbled and returns to Mount Mahendra. That meeting closes the Bala Kanda.
note.wedding.2: The painted kohbar wall is not in the text. It is the wedding custom of Mithila, the region this game's art comes from.
note.yajna.1: After Tataka, Valmiki has the sage give Rama a long list of divine weapons, which appear before him in bodily form. At Siddhashrama the princes guard the altar for six days and nights.
note.yajna.2: Rama strikes Maricha with the Manava astra, which throws him far out to sea without killing him, and destroys Subahu with the Agneya astra. Maricha returns much later, as the golden deer.
place.ravanaCourt.sub: The hall of the ten-headed king
ravana.1: Rama stands on the field, tired, thinking. The sage Agastya has come to watch the battle with the gods. He walks over.
ravana.2: Listen. There is an old prayer to the Sun, the heart of Aditya. Say it three times, facing him. It ends fear.
ravana.3: Rama says it. The Sun, looking down, says one word: hurry.
ravana.4: Indra sends you his chariot, his armour and his spear. You should not meet him on foot. I am Matali. I will drive.
ravana.boon: The heads grow back. Fill the sun with headshots.
ravana.bossIntro: Ravana: ten heads, twenty arms, and nothing left to lose
ravana.end.1: His colour drains away slowly, until he is only line.
ravana.end.2: Flowers fall on the field out of a clear sky.
ravana.matali: Matali: "Why do you fight as if you did not know? Use the weapon of Brahma."
ravana.rule: Aim for the head in colour
ravana.tip: Only the head in colour can be hurt. Headshots fill the sun: he cannot be ended until it is full.
ravana.wall.title: The Demon-King's Court
ravana.win.1: Ravana has fallen to the Brahma astra.
rekha.1: At the hut, the cry comes through the trees. Sita is on her feet before it ends.
rekha.10: An ascetic in saffron comes down the path, with a staff and a water pot, chanting.
rekha.12: A guest stands at your door, lady, and he has eaten nothing today.
rekha.13: At the line he stops as if he had walked into a wall. It flares white.
rekha.15: I have taken a vow not to enter a house. Will you send a hungry man away from it?
rekha.16: A guest who asks at the door must be fed. It is the first duty of a house, and she has kept it all her life.
rekha.17: She steps across with the food in her hands. The line goes out.
rekha.18: The saffron falls away. Ten heads, gold and black.
rekha.19: The Pushpaka rises over the trees.
rekha.2: That was his voice. Go to him. Why are you standing there?
rekha.20: Trees of Janasthana! River Godavari! Deer, birds, all of you: tell Rama. Tell him Ravana has taken me.
rekha.3: Nothing in the three worlds can hurt him. That was a trick. He told me to stay with you, and I will.
rekha.4: You will stand here while he dies. I see what you are. You have waited for this.
rekha.5: It is a terrible thing to say, and she is too frightened to hear herself say it. He stands as if she had struck him.
rekha.6: I will go. May the gods of this forest keep you. I do not think I am doing right.
rekha.7: As Lakshmana, draw the line around the hut
rekha.8: Do not step over this line. Whatever comes, it cannot cross it.
rekha.9: The line shines a little in the empty clearing. The forest goes quiet. The birds leave the sky.
rekha.grab: His hand closes on her arm. She is not lifted easily: she twists, she pulls, she strikes at the ten faces.
rekha.taken: But he has arms enough to hold a mountain, and one by one they close around her. The ground leaves her feet.
sage.1: Ayodhya, on the river Sarayu. King Dasharatha sits in his court with his four sons behind him.
sage.10: You gave your word and now you take it back. That is not the way of your house.
sage.11: Keep your promise, my king. This sage knows every weapon the gods have made. Rama will be safer with him than here.
sage.12: Then I was wrong to be afraid.
sage.13: It is hard to say, and I will say it. Take him, with my blessing.
sage.14: Well spoken. This sage knows every weapon the gods have made. No harm will come to the boy.
sage.15: Where my brother goes, I go.
sage.16: Go, both of you. Do as he tells you.
sage.17: They leave the city on foot, the sage in front, the two princes behind with their bows.
sage.2: A guard runs in. The sage Vishvamitra is at the gate.
sage.3: Great sage, your coming is like rain on a dry field. Ask, and it is yours.
sage.4: I am holding a sacrifice. Two rakshasas, Maricha and Subahu, foul the altar each time.
sage.5: Give me your eldest son, Rama, for ten nights. He will guard it.
sage.7: "He is only a boy. Take my army instead."
sage.9: He is not yet sixteen. He has never seen a battle. I will come myself, with every soldier I have.
sage.win.1: Rama and Lakshmana leave Ayodhya with the sage.
sala.1: Forgive me. I believe you mean it. But look: that is the body of the buffalo-demon Dundubhi. Vali killed him with his hands and threw him a full league.
sala.3: Rama lifts it with one toe and sends it ten leagues, out of sight.
sala.4: It was fresh when Vali threw it. It is dry now, and light. I am sorry. I have been afraid for a long time.
sala.6: Those seven sala trees. Vali can shake the leaves off one. Put an arrow through one.
sala.7: The arrow goes through all seven, and the hill behind them, and into the earth, and comes back to his quiver.
sala.hint: Hold a full draw. Release when the seven marks line up.
sala.miss: It stops in a trunk. Wait for all seven.
sala.win.1: One arrow, seven trees. Sugriva believes.
sanjeevani.1: North. Lanka, the sea, Kishkindha, Panchavati, Chitrakuta, the Ganga: the whole road back, in the time it takes to say it.
sanjeevani.10: He sits up, looks around at all the faces, and asks whether Ravana is dead yet.
sanjeevani.11: If you had not come back, I would not have wanted Sita, or victory, or my life.
sanjeevani.2: The mountain of herbs. They shine at night. They also know when someone has come to pick them.
sanjeevani.4: It goes dark as he reaches for it.
sanjeevani.6: They are hiding from him. There is no time for this.
sanjeevani.7: Then I will not choose. Sushena can choose.
sanjeevani.9: Sushena crushes a leaf and holds it under Lakshmana's nose.
sanjeevani.dawn: The sky is too light. Again, faster.
sanjeevani.hint: Fly up and down. Every hit costs time.
sarayu.1: The south bank of the Sarayu. The sage stops where the water runs clear.
sarayu.10: Must I kill a woman, master?
sarayu.11: A prince protects his people, whatever shape the danger takes. That is the whole of it.
sarayu.12: Then I will do as you say.
sarayu.2: Take water in your hands, Rama. I will give you two mantras, Bala and Atibala.
sarayu.3: With them you will not tire, or hunger, or be caught asleep.
sarayu.4: They sleep that night on grass by the river. In the morning a boat takes them over the Ganga.
sarayu.5: Before we go further, show me your arm. Three marks. Hit them.
sarayu.6: Good. A full draw goes through more than one thing. Remember that.
sarayu.7: Ahead the forest turns grey. No bird calls.
sarayu.8: There were villages here. Where are the people?
sarayu.9: Gone. A yakshini named Tataka took this country. She has the strength of a thousand elephants, and she eats what she catches.
sarayu.win.1: The princes have the mantras, and the road leads into the waste.
scroll.body: A new door, in kachni line: the longer story of Ravana, told from his side. It will open in a later version.
scroll.title: The Ravana Scroll
search.1: The rains come. No army can move. Rama waits in a cave on Mount Prasravana and watches the water fall.
search.10: Hanuman. I think it will be you. Take my ring. She will know it, and she will know you came from me.
search.11: The southern party finds nothing. Thirsty, they follow wet birds into a cave, and are lost in the dark.
search.13: No one who enters this cave leaves it alive. But you are on a good errand. Eat. Then close your eyes, and I will set you outside.
search.14: They open their eyes on the southern shore. The month is over. The sea is in front of them.
search.15: Sugriva will kill us for coming back with nothing. Let us sit here and fast until we die. Jatayu died better than this, fighting for her.
search.17: Who speaks of Jatayu? Who says my brother is dead?
search.18: I am Sampati. I burned my wings shielding him from the sun when we were young. I cannot fly, but I can still see. She is in Lanka, a hundred yojanas over that water, in a garden, weeping.
search.19: I can leap a hundred yojanas. I am not sure I can leap back.
search.20: Hanuman, why are you sitting there saying nothing? You are the son of the Wind. As a child you jumped at the sun, taking it for a fruit. You were cursed to forget your strength until someone reminded you. I am reminding you.
search.22: I could carry Lanka back by its roots. Wait here for me.
search.3: "The clouds are carrying the sea up the mountain like tired porters."
search.4: "She is somewhere under this same rain."
search.5: "The rivers have forgotten their banks. Sugriva has forgotten his promise."
search.6: The sky clears. The geese come back.
search.7: Autumn, and no word from Kishkindha. Lakshmana goes down with his bow strung. It is Tara who comes out to meet him.
search.8: He has been drunk on being safe. He is not false. The armies were sent for ten days ago. Come in and see.
search.9: They come in their millions. Sugriva sends them east, west, north and south, with one month to search.
search.win.1: Sita is in Lanka, and Hanuman remembers who he is.
set.resetAsk: Erase all progress and seals? Settings are kept.
set.toggle: Tap to draw, tap to release
set.toggleDraw: Tap to draw, tap to release
shabari.1: On the road south a thing with no head and a mouth in its belly closes its arms around them both.
shabari.10: Pampa in spring. The lotuses are open, the bees are loud, and everything that is beautiful hurts him.
shabari.11: She would have loved this lake, Lakshmana.
shabari.2: They cut themselves free, one arm each. It thanks them. It was a gandharva once, and a curse has just ended.
shabari.3: Burn this body, and I will tell you what I know. Go to the monkey Sugriva on Mount Rishyamukha. He has lost what you have lost. And on the way, by Lake Pampa, an old woman is waiting for you.
shabari.4: Shabari was a girl when her teacher Matanga told her: stay here; Rama will come. She is very old now. She has swept the path every day.
shabari.5: You have come. He said you would. Sit. I have only fruit, but I have chosen it.
shabari.6: She brings him the sweet ones in her two hands. He eats them all.
shabari.7: I have eaten at kings' tables. I have not been fed like this.
shabari.8: Then I have done what I stayed for. With your leave, I will go to my teacher now.
shabari.9: She walks into her fire as into a doorway, and they see her rise from it, young, and go up.
shabari.pick: Tap a berry to taste it
shabari.sour: Sour. Tap the basket to set it aside.
shabari.sweet: Sweet. Tap the basket for Rama.
shabari.wasSour: That one was sour. She takes it back.
shabari.wasSweet: That one was sweet. She gives it to him after all.
shabari.win.1: Shabari's waiting is over. The road leads to Kishkindha.
shurpanakha.1: A winter morning at Panchavati. A rakshasi walking by the river sees Rama, and stops.
shurpanakha.10: She looks from one to the other, and understands that she is being laughed at.
shurpanakha.11: It is her. While she lives you will not look at me.
shurpanakha.12: Lakshmana! Stop her. This has gone past a joke.
shurpanakha.13: There is a cry. She covers her face with her cloth and runs, north, toward Janasthana, where her brother Khara keeps an army.
shurpanakha.14: She will not come back alone.
shurpanakha.2: I am Shurpanakha, sister of Ravana, and I go where I please. I have chosen you. Leave that thin human girl. Be my husband.
shurpanakha.4: Tease her: "I am married. But my brother there has no wife with him."
shurpanakha.5: Refuse her plainly: "I am married, and I am content."
shurpanakha.6: I have a wife, lady, and you would not like to be the second. But my brother there has no wife with him.
shurpanakha.7: I am married, and I am content. You must look elsewhere.
shurpanakha.8: Then the younger one will do.
shurpanakha.9: I am my brother's servant. Would you be a servant's wife? Go back to him. He may yet change his mind.
shurpanakha.win.1: Shurpanakha runs to her brother Khara.
tataka.bossIntro: The yakshini comes roaring out of the dust
tataka.cp1: Lakshmana: "She is close. I can smell the dust."
tataka.end.1: Vishvamitra: "Now this country can be lived in again."
tataka.lose.tip: Watch the ground. The lotus means jump; the shadow-star means she will rise there.
tataka.win.1: Tataka falls, and the wasteland can be lived in again.
tataka.win.2: Pleased, Vishvamitra prepares to give Rama the divine astras.
tip.general: Watch for the painted signs: a star means a blow, a lotus means jump.
tip.jump: A lotus opening on the ground, or a dust line, means jump.
tip.kick: Stand near a climber and Rama kicks it off the cliff.
tip.move: A red hatched circle or a dotted red path shows where it will land. Step out of it.
tip.protect: Stay near what you are guarding.
tip.roll: A painted star means a blow is coming. Roll through it.
tip.shoot: Shoot it before it reaches you. A full draw hits harder.
tip.timer: Too slow. Use full draws and keep moving forward.
tip.watch: A painted star means a blow is coming: roll through it.

vali.1: Sugriva goes to the gate of Kishkindha and roars for his brother. Vali comes out.
vali.10: Vali listens. Whether he is satisfied, the poem does not quite say. He says: I should not have spoken so.
vali.11: Sugriva. Look after Angada. He is a boy. Rama, he is yours now too.
vali.12: He takes the gold necklace Indra gave him from his own neck, puts it on his brother, and dies.
vali.13: Sugriva is crowned king of the vanaras, and Angada crown prince. Rama, who may not enter a city, watches from the hill.
vali.2: From the trees Rama watches two golden monkeys fight, alike as the two Ashvins. He cannot tell which is which, and does not shoot.
vali.3: You watched him break me! Was this the help you swore?
vali.4: I could not tell you apart. If I had killed you, what would my oath be worth? Go again. This time I will know you.
vali.5: Lakshmana pulls up a flowering creeper and hangs it around Sugriva's neck.
vali.6: He was beaten an hour ago and he is back, shouting. He has found someone. The sons of Dasharatha are in this forest. Make peace with your brother.
vali.7: I will not kill him. I will only take the pride out of him. Do not be afraid.
vali.8: I was fighting another, and my back was to you. I had no quarrel with you. They say you are just. Why did you shoot from hiding?
vali.9: You took your brother's wife while he lived. This land answers to the kings of my house, and a king must punish that. I punished it.
vali.hint: Sugriva wears the garland. Draw, wait, and shoot only Vali.
vali.miss: That was Sugriva. The duel begins again.
vali.win.1: Vali is dead. Sugriva is king.
vali.wrong: Not yet! That was not a clear shot. The brothers close again.
viradha.1: The Dandaka forest. Hermits come out of the trees to meet them, thin men who carry no weapons.
viradha.10: You knew what I wanted before I said it. It is as if our father were still alive.
viradha.11: An old vulture, very large, settles on the banyan and looks at them with one eye, then the other.
viradha.13: I am Jatayu. I flew with your father when we were both young. When you two go hunting, I will watch over Sita.
viradha.2: Look at that heap, prince. Those are the bones of our brothers. The rakshasas eat us at our prayers.
viradha.3: You should not have to ask. I am ashamed that you had to. They will not trouble you again while I live.
viradha.4: You have given your word to men who did not fight. Be careful with the bow, my lord. Carrying it changes the one who carries it.
viradha.5: I hear you. But I have promised, and you know what I am about promises.
viradha.6: Sharabhanga has put off his own death until he could see Rama. He blesses him, and walks into his fire.
viradha.7: Ten years go by among the hermitages. A month here, a season there. They are the quiet years.
viradha.8: This bow was Vishnu's. These two quivers never empty. You will need them. Go to Panchavati, on the Godavari. It is a good place.
viradha.9: At Panchavati Lakshmana builds a hut of bamboo and leaves, alone, in a day.
viradha.archer: The dotted red path shows the shot: step out of it
viradha.bossIntro: Viradha bursts from the trees and seizes Sita
viradha.cp: Sita: "Something large is moving in the trees."
viradha.end.1: They dig a pit, as he asks, and bury him.
viradha.end.2: A gandharva rises from the earth, freed: "Go to the sage Sharabhanga. He is waiting for you."
viradha.rule: Arrows do nothing to his body. Shoot a shoulder when he swings.
viradha.tip: His arms are the only way. Roll through the swing, then shoot a shoulder.
viradha.win.1: Viradha, whom no weapon could kill, is buried and freed.
wedding.1: Dasharatha rides into Mithila with Bharata and Shatrughna, four days after the riders left.
wedding.10: The sun and the moon, as witnesses
wedding.11: And four veiled naina-jogins in the corners, to keep watch
wedding.12: There. Now it is a wall that has seen a wedding.
wedding.13: On the road home the wind turns and the birds scatter. A man with an axe stands in the way.
wedding.14: I am Parashurama. I heard a bow break. You broke Shiva's, which was old and tired. Here is Vishnu's. String it, and I will fight you. Fail, and you will kneel.
wedding.15: He is a boy, newly married. Let him pass.
wedding.17: Hold to draw Vishnu's bow. Release when the ring is full.
wedding.18: It is strung and it is drawn. An arrow on this bow cannot be put back. Tell me where it should go.
wedding.19: Not at me. I know now who holds it. Let it take my pride, and I will go back to the mountain.
wedding.2: I have two daughters, and my brother has two. You have four sons. Let us not do this by halves.
wedding.20: They come into Ayodhya together, four sons and four brides, and the city comes out to the road.
wedding.3: Four weddings around one fire. Rama and Sita. Lakshmana and Urmila. Bharata and Mandavi. Shatrughna and Shrutakirti.
wedding.4: This is Sita, my daughter. Take her hand in yours. She will walk with you like your shadow.
wedding.5: In the bridal room the women of Mithila paint the wall, as they have always done. Sita holds out each piece.
wedding.6: Drag each motif to its place
wedding.7: The lotus pierced by bamboo, at the centre
wedding.win.1: Four weddings, one painted wall, and the road home.
yajna.1: Morning. The sage is smiling, which is rare.
yajna.2: You did what I asked, and you took no joy in it. Sit facing east, Rama. I have weapons to give you.
yajna.3: He speaks their names, and the astras come: shining figures standing in a ring around the prince, waiting to be called.
yajna.4: An astra is called by its sign. Draw it clean and it answers in full. Draw the sun.
yajna.5: They are yours. Think of them, and they will come.
yajna.6: Siddhashrama. The sage takes a vow of silence. For six days and six nights he will not speak, and the fire must not go out.
yajna.bossIntro: Maricha and Subahu darken the sky above the altar
yajna.end.1: Vishvamitra: "The rite is whole. You have kept your father's word and mine."
yajna.flung: The wind astra flings Maricha far out to sea
yajna.tip: Stand near the altar. Shoot the ones who run for the fire first.
yajna.up: Aim high: shoot them as they dive
yajna.win.2: Maricha, flung a hundred yojanas out to sea, lives. He will remember Rama.
